definition.given: A GLPI administrator is editing the Service request details form. Its Summary short-answer question has one validation criterion, length greater than 5, and one visibility criterion, Category equals Assistance. The validation and visibility badges each display 1.
definition.when: Inspect the Summary validation editor without changing its criterion. Open the Summary visibility editor, delete its sole criterion using Delete criteria, and close the editor without saving the form.
definition.observed: After the visibility criterion is deleted, both Summary count badges display 0. The validation criterion inspected earlier was not edited or deleted, yet its badge also changes from 1 to 0. The recording demonstrates the unsaved editor state; it does not demonstrate persistence after saving or reloading.
definition.require: After deleting the sole visibility criterion and closing its editor, retain Summary's length-greater-than-5 validation rule. Show validation count 1 and visibility count 0 without saving or reloading.
allow: Equivalent placement, styling, or wording of the two count indicators is acceptable if their validation and visibility meanings and counts remain clear.
No requirement is imposed on the exact DOM structure, internal event handling, or persistence beyond this unsaved editing sequence.

theory.title: Visual clarity and faithful state communication
theory.reference: Jenifer Tidwell, Charles Brewer, and Aynne Valencia, Designing Interfaces, Third Edition; Chapter 5: Visual Style and Aesthetics. Conceptual application based on chapter synthesis.
theory.rationale: The skill's synthesis treats visual design as functional communication. These separately labeled badges summarize two different rule categories. Reporting zero validation criteria after only a visibility criterion was removed gives the administrator false information about the question's validation state. Keeping each count faithful to its own category makes the form understandable and supports reliable editing.

reference_observation: Deleting Summary's sole visibility criterion leaves its validation badge at 1 and changes its visibility badge to 0. The length-greater-than-5 validation criterion remains unchanged. The form is neither saved nor reloaded.
requirement_rationale: Validation determines acceptable answers; visibility determines when a question is shown. Their badges summarize independent rule sets, so removing a visibility rule must not make the remaining validation rule appear absent.
